title: Asymptotic Compression of Interactive Quantum Communication using Type-Constrained de Finetti Reduction
authors: Louis Desruisseaux, Simon Ducharme, Gurleen Padda, Dave Touchette
abstract: For many information processing tasks, de Finetti-style theorems can often simplify the analysis in worst-case input scenarios for which the task exhibits some permutation-invariance symmetry, as they can allow for a reduction from an analysis on worst-case inputs to that of i.i.d. inputs. If further information is available on the inputs, it might be advantageous to reflect this information in the de Finetti reduction. In our work, we focus on a form of such constraint, based on the type of the input. This allows us to obtain a conceptually simple proof of a new de Finetti reduction for classical probability distributions, derived from elementary properties from the method of types. We apply our constrained de Finetti reduction to the compression of quantum interactive communication protocols with classical inputs, and prove that the prior-free quantum information cost equals the worst-case input amortized quantum communication cost.
summary: The paper proves that the fundamental rate of communication capacity in interactive quantum protocols is determined equally by two measures: the Quantum Information Cost and the Amortized Quantum Communication Complexity. This equivalence is achieved using a novel type-constrained de Finetti reduction, which simplifies complex worst-case analysis into manageable i.i.d. bounds.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish an equivalence between two fundamental measures of communication capacity: the prior-free quantum information cost (QIC) and the prior-free amortized quantum communication complexity (AQCC). This addresses a long-standing open question in quantum information theory.
main_result: It proves that for interactive quantum communication protocols with classical inputs, the Quantum Information Cost equals the Amortized Quantum Communication Complexity ($	ext{QIC}(\Pi) = 	ext{AQCC}(\Pi)$).
method: The core methodology involves developing and applying a novel type-constrained de Finetti reduction to simplify complex worst-case input analyses into tractable i.i.d. settings.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum interactive communication protocols involving multiple rounds of communication, where the inputs are classical sequences drawn from fixed alphabets. The mathematical framework utilizes density operators and tensor products over Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: Quantum Information Cost ($	ext{QIC}$), Amortized Quantum Communication Complexity ($	ext{AQCC}$), total quantum communication cost ($QCC$), and various conditional mutual information terms.
important_parameters: The asymptotic limit ($n 	o \infty$) is crucial, as are the approximation parameters $\delta$ (controlling typicality) and the structure of the classical inputs/types.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the protocols operate with classical inputs drawn from fixed alphabets and relies heavily on bounding errors using $\delta$-typical sets derived from de Finetti's theorem.
figures_summary: Figure 4 illustrates the general structure of an interactive quantum communication protocol involving multiple rounds ($r$) with classical inputs, which is the system under analysis.
paper_structure: The paper builds logically by first establishing the type-constrained de Finetti reduction for classical distributions (Chunk 1). It then applies this to bound channel norms and state approximations (Chunks 2 & 7), culminating in simulating the full interactive protocol using these bounds to prove the final equivalence $	ext{QIC}(\Pi) = 	ext{AQCC}(\Pi)$ (Chunks 3, 5, & 6).
why_interesting: This work provides deep theoretical tools—the type-constrained de Finetti reduction—that bridge classical probability theory with quantum information bounds, offering a powerful new technique for analyzing resource theories.
